newsitem.title: USA: Pennsylvania Real Estate buys co, property.
newsitem.headline: Pennsylvania Real Estate buys co, property.

text.p: Pennsylvania Real Estate Investment Trust said Thursday it has a definitive agreement to acquire Rubin Organization, a full-service real estate company, and interests in a number of shopping centers for an estimated $260 million.

As part of the deal, Pennsylvania Real Estate would acquire interests in four existing shopping centers and two shopping centers nearing completion totaling about 2.9 million square feet, plus interests in four potential shopping center development projects.
In addition, Pennsylvania Real Estate said it will begin conducting its operations through an umbrella partnership real estate investment trust.
Pennsylvania Real Estate said it will contribute its real estate interests to a newly formed operating partnership, of which it will be the sole general partner.

The newly formed operating partnership would acquire 95 percent of the equity of the Rubin Organization in exchange for the issuance of 200,000 operating partnership units and a provision to issue up to 800,000 additional operating partnership units over the next five years.

Pennsylvania Real Estate Chairman and Chief Executive Sylvan Cohen said in a statement that the company expects the "acquisition of the completed properties and the management company to be immediately accretive to PREIT's FFO (funds from operations) per share and to contribute significantly to FFO per share growth in 1998 and in future years."
Following the acquisition, Ronald Rubin, founder and chief executive officer of Rubin Organization, would become chief executive of Pennsylvania Real Estate Investment Trust.
Cohen will continue to serve as chairman. Jonathan Weller will continue to serve as president and chief operating officer of Pennsylvania Real Estate Investment Trust.
Immediately following the close of the transaction, Pennsylvania Real Estate officers would beneficially own about 13 percent of the shares/units outstanding, it said.

The company said that management's ownership could increase to more than 20 percent, depending upon several factors, including the trust's achievement of certain specified levels of FFO over the next five years.
The acquisition is expected to be completed by September 30. At that time, Pennsylvania Real Estate said it would consider changing its fiscal year end to December 31 from August 31.
